category.source: Inferred from callout labels (zipper, handle, modular zipper) in the supplied LAGI graphic. Not confirmed by brand.

observations.label: Supplied asset is a callout/label graphic ("LAGI — LOOK CLOSER") with three annotation markers, not a product photograph.
Callout labels read: "ZIPPER DETAIL — smooth operation, everyday durability", "HANDLE DETAIL — durable webbing, comfortable grip", "MODULAR ZIPPER — changeable, expandable system".
Product referenced is a bag-type item with a zipper closure, a webbing handle, and a modular/expandable zipper system.
Actual product photograph, silhouette, proportions, color, and full construction are not present in the supplied asset.

A reference photo was later supplied showing a structured box tote: cream/white body, blue top-edge trim, yellow piping down the left edge, a green zipper trim down the right edge, two red vertical webbing stripes on the front continuing up into a double-loop red handle, and a yellow cam-buckle adjuster on the handle webbing.

model3D (lagi-bag.glb) is a hand-built low-poly approximation of that reference photo's visible silhouette and trim colors — not a photogrammetry scan or AI reconstruction, and no internal/hidden construction was inferred or modeled.

A follow-up reference sheet ("LAGI BAG 01 — 3D MODEL SPEC FOR WEB AR") was supplied with multi-angle views (front/back/left/right/top/open interior), an exploded parts diagram, and an explicit color legend: Ivory Canvas, Red Strap, Blue Trim, Yellow Zipper, Green Edge, Beige Interior.

model3D (lagi-bag.glb) was rebuilt against that spec sheet with named, separable node groups — MainBody, FrontPocket, Straps, Handles, Zipper, OpeningTop, Interior — for future per-part interaction, using the sheet's exact color legend. It remains a hand-built low-poly approximation (flat-color primitives, no photogrammetry/AI reconstruction, no fabric stitching or texture detail).

The original real-photo reference (structured cream tote, red webbing straps/handle, blue top trim, green side edges, yellow buckle) was set as the primary reference over the spec-sheet diagram at the requester's direction. model3D (lagi-bag.glb) was rebuilt a third time to raise realism: soft-rounded body edges (not a sharp box), procedurally generated fabric-weave and webbing textures baked into the GLB (not flat colors), dashed stitch-line geometry at seams, individually modeled zipper teeth + a separate metal-look slider/pull, and metal-finish hardware (buckle, rivets). Node groups now match the requested interaction parts: MainBody, FrontPocket, LeftSidePanel, RightSidePanel, Straps, Handles, Zipper, Zipper_Slider, OpeningTop, InteriorLining, InnerPocket, Hardware.

This is still a hand-authored approximation, not a photogrammetry scan or AI 3D reconstruction (no such tool is available in this environment) — no true cloth simulation/draping, no exact zipper-coil profile, and no baked brand wordmark. Textures are procedural (generated code), not derived from pixels of the reference photos.

Proportions and part placement were measured directly off the reference sheet's orthographic views by sampling its pixels: body 206w x 183h with a 68 deep side (W:H:D = 1 : 0.889 : 0.330), constant width top to bottom, handle apex 41% of body height above the top edge, webbing 10.7% of the width at centres +-16.6%, front pocket seams at 23.5% and 54.6% of body height from the top, and a corner build-up reading green tape / yellow piping / blue tape / ivory face from the outside in.

model3D (lagi-bag.glb) was rebuilt a fourth time against those measurements, replacing the primitive-assembly approach: the shell is a single lofted super-ellipse surface, the webbing is a flat ribbon swept along a 3D path as one continuous run (front face, over the top, handle arch, back face) that is then split into named parts, the trims are strips taken off the same lofted surface, and the front pocket is a fabric shell following the body's curvature with the webbing passing behind it as in the reference. Node groups: MainBody, FrontPocket, LeftSidePanel, RightSidePanel, Straps, Handles, Zipper, Zipper_Slider, OpeningTop, InteriorLining, InnerPocket, Hardware, Piping, Stitching. The top narrows to a zipper line so an opening animation can be added later; no animation is authored yet.
